source.publisher: FATF and Egmont Group of Financial Intelligence Units
source.title: Trade-Based Money Laundering: Risk Indicators

summary: This FATF-Egmont Group advisory (March 2021) sets out risk indicators for identifying trade-based money laundering (TBML), drawn from a sample of data gathered during the FATF/Egmont TBML project. It groups indicators into four categories: structural indicators about the trade entity itself (e.g. shell companies, mass registration addresses, nominee owners concealing beneficial ownership); trade activity indicators (e.g. activity inconsistent with stated business, unreasonably low profit margins, sudden high-volume trade by newly formed entities); trade document and commodity indicators (e.g. inconsistent invoices/contracts, vague commodity descriptions, missing or falsified customs documents); and account/transaction indicators (e.g. pay-through or transit accounts, cash structured below reporting thresholds, and circular payment routing). The document states no single indicator is conclusive and indicators should be assessed against the totality of the customer and transaction profile.

citations.quote: Contracts, invoices, or other trade documents display fees or prices that do not seem to be in line with commercial considerations, are inconsistent with market value, or significantly fluctuate from previous comparable transactions.
A trade entity consistently displays unreasonably low profit margins
importing wholesale commodities at or above retail value, or re-selling commodities at the same or below purchase price

Contracts, invoices, or other trade documents display fees or prices that do not seem to be in line with commercial considerations, are inconsistent with market value, or significantly fluctuate from previous comparable transactions.
The corporate structure of a trade entity appears unusually complex and illogical, such as the involvement of shell companies
A trade entity maintains a minimal number of working staff, inconsistent with its volume of traded commodities.
An account of a trade entity appears to be a "pay-through" or "transit" account with a rapid movement of high-volume transactions and a small end-of-day balance without clear business reasons
Payments are routed in a circle – funds are sent out from one country and received back in the same country, after passing through another country or countries.
Cash deposits or other transactions of a trade entity are consistently just below relevant reporting thresholds.

Payment for imported commodities is made by an entity other than the consignee of the commodities with no clear economic reasons, e.g. by a shell or front company not involved in the trade transaction.

extraction_notes: This is a generic, non-case-specific FATF/Egmont risk-indicator advisory: it names no specific persons, organisations, vessels, wallets or jurisdictions by ISO code, so the jurisdictions list is intentionally empty and actors are limited to the two generic classes the document itself describes (criminals; trade entities used as vehicles). The document does not distinguish over- vs under-invoicing direction when describing price/margin anomalies (pages 6-7), so both TBML001 and TBML002U are linked against the same underlying text pending reviewer judgement on which direction (or both) applies. TBML008 (Third Party Payment Abuse) and TBML009 (Shell Company Trading) were returned by knowledge_centre_search_typologies at modest scores (0.26 and 0.47) but were confirmed as strong textual matches against the retrieved doctrine summaries via knowledge_centre_get_typology before linking. Several generic indicators on pages 5-8 (e.g. negative news, dormancy, non-compliance with VAT filing, missing/counterfeit customs documents, shipments routed through multiple jurisdictions without justification) were not mapped to a specific governed typology because the match to any single library entry was too weak to clear the bar for a confident link; they are omitted from both typologies and indicators per the 'fewer, well-cited items' guidance rather than forced into an ill-fitting or emergent category. Page count and citations verified against the PAGE markers in the supplied document text (PAGE 3 = printed folio 1 through PAGE 8 = printed folio 6); pages 1-2 (cover/front matter) and pages 9-10 (blank/back cover) carry no substantive citable content.
